deep.reconstruction:
This folio contains no mathematics and no handwriting by Riemann. It is page 5 of a printed Berlin University lecture catalogue (Verzeichnis der Vorlesungen der Königlichen Friedrich-Wilhelms-Universität zu Berlin). The previous page (4) and next page (6) come from the same printed booklet.

The page continues the section on medical lectures:
- Clinical exercises in ophthalmology, given by Angelstein and by Kranichfeld, who cites his 'Anthropologische Übersicht der gesammten Ophthalmiatrie', Berlin 1841.
- Obstetrics, given by Busch, Wilde and Schöller.
- The medical clinic at the Charité, given by Schönlein, plus clinics and polyclinics run by Romberg, Trüstedt, Wolff, Jüngken, Dieffenbach, Busch and Schmidt.
- The clinic for the insane, given by Ideler.
- Forensic medicine, given by Casper and Nicolai.
- Veterinary medicine, given by Reckleben.

It then opens the section 'Philosophische Wissenschaften':
- Gabler, Einleitung in die Philosophie.
- Trendelenburg, Logik, citing his 'Logische Untersuchungen'.
- Michelet, Logik und Encyklopädie.
- An entry for Logik und Encyklopädie that runs over onto p. 6 (Althaus).

The next page goes on to 'Mathematische Wissenschaften', including Steiner's geometric exercises and his course on maxima and minima of figures, and Ohm's algebra. This is presumably why Riemann kept the leaflet: it is the catalogue of a semester he spent as a student in Berlin (1847–49).

Dating evidence:
- Kranichfeld's 1841 book is cited.
- Dieffenbach is still teaching; he died on 11 November 1847.
- Schönlein, Romberg, Casper and Trendelenburg are all active.

This fits the catalogue for Summer Semester 1847, or possibly Winter 1847/48 if it was printed before Dieffenbach's death. That matches Riemann's arrival in Berlin at Easter 1847.

There are no derivations, formulas or annotations to reconstruct.

results.what: Printed university lecture announcements (medicine, start of philosophy); no mathematical content
results.modern_name: Not applicable (archival/biographical document: Berlin Vorlesungsverzeichnis, c. 1847)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a printed Berlin lecture catalogue with no mathematics and no visible annotation by Riemann. Its only interest is biographical: it documents the courses on offer when Riemann studied in Berlin, a well-known episode of his life.
transcription_corrections: The machine transcription agrees closely with the print. In the 'Repetitorien in der Geburtshülfe' entry and in the line '...im Bereiche des hiesigen gerichtlichen Stadt-Physikats', the printed lines overlap or are smeared (a press defect), so these words are partly illegible in the image; the transcription's reading is a plausible reconstruction.
In the line 'Veterinär-Poli-zei, derselbe', the image shows a stray mark after the comma; it is a printing blemish, not text.
